name: Ulysses
first: Only spacecraft ever to enter a high-inclination heliocentric orbit; only direct measurements of the solar wind at all heliographic latitudes
description: Joint ESA / NASA mission. Launched 1990-10-06 from STS-41 Discovery + IUS + PAM-S upper stages, Ulysses used a Jupiter gravity assist on 1992-02-08 to deflect itself ~80° out of the ecliptic — the only way to reach a near-polar Sun-relative orbit from Earth's near-equatorial orbital plane. Three full polar orbits of the Sun over 18.5 years mapped the solar wind, heliospheric magnetic field, and energetic particles at all heliographic latitudes — direct measurements that revealed how solar-wind structure varies between equatorial slow-wind regions and high-latitude fast-wind streams from coronal holes. Mission terminated 2009-06-30 when thruster hydrazine froze in the lines. Hardware remains in heliocentric polar orbit.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: STS-41 Discovery deploys Ulysses + IUS / PAM-S upper stages.

events.label: JUPITER FLYBY
events.note: Gravity assist deflects Ulysses ~80° out of the ecliptic into a polar Sun-relative orbit.

events.label: FIRST SOUTH POLAR PASS
events.note: First-ever direct measurements of solar wind over a Sun pole.

events.label: FIRST NORTH POLAR PASS
events.note: Completion of the first full solar polar orbit.

events.label: MISSION END
events.note: Thruster lines freeze; final command issued 2009-06-30.
